question: Refer to the exhibit. Which configuration ensures that the Cisco Nexus 7000 Series switches are the primary devices for LACP?
context: Topology: Nexus 7000 device A and device B connected via vPC Peer Keepalive and vPC Peer Link, both downstream connected (lacp 32768) to two access switches.
imageNote: Diagram: Nexus 7000 device A and device B connected by a vPC Peer Keepalive link and vPC Peer Link, each downstream connected (lacp 32768) to two access switches.
options: N7K_A(config-vpc-domain)# role priority 1 N7K_B(config-vpc-domain)# role priority 2
theory: Configuring a common, non-default vPC system-priority (lower than the default 32768 access-switch priority) on both Nexus 7000 vPC peers, combined with the shared vPC system MAC they already present, makes the two chassis appear to downstream devices as a single logical LACP system with a numerically better (lower) priority value. Since LACP prefers the lower system priority when deciding which side controls port selection, giving both N7Ks the same low system-priority (4000, well below the downstream switches' default 32768) ensures the vPC pair is elected as the LACP primary/controlling system. (CCNP/CCIE DCCOR Official Cert Guide, Chapter 2 — vPC and LACP)
